title: Runbook: Status Page Update Procedure (Oncall)
author: Tomáš Novák
body:
## Purpose
This runbook describes the end-to-end procedure for publishing customer-facing updates on the public status page during an incident, including:
- Selecting the correct status components (and regions) based on impact
- Posting updates using standard phases and language
- Linking the public incident to the internal incident ID
- Meeting update cadence expectations
- Triggering (and completing) the customer-facing post-incident summary workflow

This procedure applies to **Sev1+** incidents by default, and to **Sev2** incidents when customer impact is visible or Support/CS requests a status page entry.

---

## Preconditions / Access
You will need:
- Status page publisher access (see: External Comms Approval Policy)
- Slack access to **#incidents** and **incident-bot**
- The internal incident record (PagerDuty incident + internal incident doc) and incident ID (e.g., **INC-2024-0812-043**) 

If you do not have status page access:
1) Ask the Incident Commander (IC) to publish, OR
2) Page the SRE lead on duty for publishing support.

---

## Definitions (customer-facing)
Use consistent language aligned with our templates:
- **Investigating**: We see a problem and are actively triaging.
- **Identified**: We believe we know the cause and are working on mitigation.
- **Monitoring**: Mitigation applied; we’re watching metrics to confirm recovery.
- **Resolved**: We believe service is restored and will continue monitoring internally.

Impact wording:
- **Degraded performance**: higher latency, intermittent errors, reduced throughput, elevated 429s.
- **Partial outage**: a subset of requests failing (specific route/model/region/streaming).
- **Major outage**: widespread failure across primary customer paths.

See: Customer Impact Classification.

---

## Step-by-step procedure

### 1) Confirm we should publish (and when)
1) Determine severity and customer visibility.
2) If **Sev1/Sev0**: publish immediately.
3) If **Sev2**: publish if:
   - Many customers likely impacted, OR
   - Any enterprise customer impacted, OR
   - Support is receiving multiple tickets, OR
   - The issue may last >15 minutes.
4) If you are unsure, publish a short **Investigating** update with scoped components and clear uncertainty language.

Guiding principle: Customers prefer a timely, scoped update over silence.

---

### 2) Identify the correct components (and scope)
Select components that reflect **what customers experience**, not internal services.

#### 2.1 Component selection checklist
- What product surface is affected?
  - Hosted API routes (Chat/Generate), **Streaming**, **Embeddings**, **Rerank**
  - Console
  - Dedicated Control Plane
  - Private Control Plane
  - Capacity & Routing (when requests can’t be scheduled/routed reliably)
- Is the impact **regional**?
  - Use regional components (e.g., Hosted API Serving (us-east)) when impact is clearly region-bound.
- Is the impact **route-specific**?
  - Streaming-only failures should use **Streaming** (and possibly Hosted API Serving if non-streaming is also affected).
- Is the impact **model-family specific**?
  - If a specific model family is failing across multiple routes, use the route component(s) plus a note in the update body (do not create ad-hoc components).

#### 2.2 Mapping rules (quick)
- Prefer **multiple components** over one broad component if it increases customer clarity.
- Do not expose internal names (clusters, schedulers, hostnames, vendor ticket IDs).
- If the “blast radius” is uncertain, start narrow and expand as confirmed.

Examples:
- Only streaming disconnects elevated; non-streaming OK → mark **Streaming** as Degraded.
- 5xx on /v1/embeddings in eu-west only → mark **Embeddings** and **Hosted API Serving (eu-west)**.
- Console loads but incident banner missing → mark **Console**.
- Dedicated deployments can’t scale or deploy → mark **Dedicated Control Plane**.

See: Status Page Component Taxonomy + Mapping Guidelines.

---

### 3) Create the status page incident and link the internal incident ID
1) In incident-bot (Slack), run the status page helper:
   - Command: `/incident status start` (or use the incident-bot incident menu → “Status page update”)
2) Enter:
   - Internal incident ID (required): `INC-YYYY-MMDD-###`
   - Severity (internal)
   - Customer-facing title (see guidance below)
   - Affected components + regions
   - Current phase: Investigating
   - Next update time (required)
3) incident-bot will:
   - Generate a draft using the standard template for the phase
   - Include the internal incident ID in the “Internal reference” field (or top of draft body where supported)
   - Post a preview in Slack for quick review

If incident-bot is unavailable:
- Create the incident manually in the status page console.
- Add the internal incident ID to the update body as: `Internal reference: INC-YYYY-MMDD-###`.

#### 3.1 Customer-facing incident title guidance
Use: “<Product surface> <impact>” + optional region.
Good:
- “Streaming degraded performance (us-east)”
- “Embeddings partial outage (eu-west)”
- “Hosted API elevated 5xx errors”
Avoid:
- “Scheduler regression in gke-prod-7”
- “Redis saturation”

---

### 4) Publish the initial update (Investigating)
Publish the initial update as soon as there is confirmed customer impact. Keep it short and actionable.

Required elements (at least 2):
- What’s impacted (components + symptom)
- Who is impacted (subset/region/route) if known
- What customers can do now (mitigation/workaround) if safe
- When the next update will be posted

Use template language:
- “We are investigating reports of …”
- “Impact appears limited to …” (if uncertain, say so)
- “Next update by <time> <timezone>.”

Customer actions (only if accurate):
- Retry with exponential backoff
- Switch from streaming to non-streaming (or vice versa) if applicable
- Temporarily pin to an alternate region (if supported for that customer)
- Use a fallback model (if customers have configured fallbacks)

Never instruct customers to do anything that increases platform load (e.g., tight retry loops).

---

### 5) Ongoing updates (Identified / Monitoring)
#### 5.1 Update cadence
Follow: Status Page Update SLA & Cadence.
Default expectations:
- Sev0: first update ASAP; then every **15–30 minutes**
- Sev1: first update ASAP; then every **30–60 minutes**
- Sev2 (published): every **60–120 minutes** while ongoing

If there is no material change:
- Still post an update on schedule with what we have learned, what we are doing, and reaffirm the next update time.

#### 5.2 Phase transition guidance
- Move to **Identified** when we have high confidence in the cause category and are actively mitigating.
- Move to **Monitoring** after mitigation is applied and leading indicators are improving.
- Move to **Resolved** only after:
  - customer-facing metrics return to baseline, AND
  - the team agrees the issue is no longer actively impacting customers.

#### 5.3 What to include in each phase
Investigating:
- Symptom + scope + uncertainty language
Identified:
- What we believe is causing impact (high-level, customer-safe)
- Mitigation steps in progress
Monitoring:
- Mitigation applied + what metrics look like + what we’re watching
Resolved:
- Confirmation of recovery + note that a post-incident summary will follow for Sev1/Sev0

---

### 6) Component adjustments during an incident
Update components if the blast radius changes.

Rules of thumb:
- If impact expands: update components immediately and state “We have updated affected components based on new information.”
- If impact narrows: only remove components once metrics and logs support the change.
- Avoid flip-flopping: prefer “appears limited to …” language when uncertain.

Common edge cases:
- Streaming degraded vs API degraded:
  - If streaming-only: mark **Streaming**.
  - If both streaming and non-streaming fail: mark **Streaming** + **Hosted API Serving**.
- Region ambiguity:
  - If the issue appears region-bound but uncertain: start with the most likely region component and explicitly call out uncertainty.
  - If multi-region: use each impacted region component (avoid a single global component unless truly global).

---

### 7) Approval workflow (when required)
Most Sev1 operational incidents can be published by the oncall publisher without additional approvals.

Escalate for review before publishing if updates include:
- Security events, suspected exploitation, data exposure risk
- Customer-specific impacts (names, identifiers)
- Provider/legal constraints or sensitive dependency details
- Any statement that changes contractual commitments

Approval path (typical):
- SRE lead on duty → Security/Compliance (Dr. Aisha Rahman / Marcus Lin) → Legal/Privacy (Michael Grant) as needed

See: External Comms Approval Policy.

---

### 8) Resolve the status page incident
When resolving:
1) Post a **Resolved** update.
2) Confirm components are set back to Operational.
3) Include the internal incident ID in the final update if it wasn’t included earlier.
4) Trigger the post-incident summary workflow (next section).

---

## Post-incident summary workflow (customer-facing)
We publish a customer-facing post-incident summary for **Sev1 and Sev0** incidents (and Sev2 when requested by Support/CS or enterprise customers).

### 9) Trigger summary generation (T+0)
Immediately after resolving:
1) In incident-bot: `/incident summary start`
2) Select the incident (by internal incident ID).
3) incident-bot will create a summary stub and link it in:
   - the internal incident channel
   - the incident record
   - the status page incident (internal references section where supported)

### 10) Complete and publish the summary (SLA)
SLA targets (business days):
- Sev0/Sev1: publish within **3 business days**
- Sev2 (if published): within **5 business days** or per enterprise request

Summary should align with the internal postmortem but be customer-safe:
Include:
- Impact (what users saw, which components/regions)
- Timeline (start, mitigation applied, recovery)
- Root cause category (high-level)
- Mitigation and prevention (what we changed / will change)
- Where customers can learn more (status page incident link)

Do NOT include:
- Customer names or identifiable customer traffic patterns
- Exploit or vulnerability-like detail
- Internal-only system names that meaningfully aid attackers
- Provider ticket IDs or contract-sensitive statements

Use: Post-Incident Summary Template.

### 11) Reminders and ownership
- incident-bot will remind the assigned owner at **T+1** and **T+3** business days.
- If the owner is unavailable, the IC assigns a delegate (usually SRE oncall lead).

---

## Quality bar (before you hit Publish)
Quick checklist:
- Components selected match customer symptoms (not internal services)
- Region scope correct (or uncertainty clearly stated)
- Update includes a next update time
- Language is customer-safe and avoids internal jargon
- No sensitive details (security, customer identifiers, exploitation hints)
- Update is not empty: includes at least one of {impact, mitigation/workaround, next update time}

---

## Reference: Copy-ready snippets (approved)
Use these as-is when helpful.

Uncertainty:
- “We are still investigating and will share more as we confirm the scope.”
- “Impact appears limited to <component/region>, but we are continuing to validate.”

Mitigation in progress:
- “We are applying a mitigation to restore normal service and will update as metrics improve.”

Monitoring:
- “A mitigation has been deployed and we are monitoring recovery. We will provide another update by <time>.”

Resolved + summary expectation:
- “This incident is resolved. For Sev1/Sev0 incidents, we will publish a post-incident summary within 3 business days.”

---

## Troubleshooting
- incident-bot draft-sync not posting:
  - Check feature flag status in #eng-releases
  - Publish manually and note the internal incident ID
- Status page component missing:
  - Use the closest matching component and file a follow-up in the Linear epic (Status page transparency upgrades)
- Disagreement on scope/components:
  - Default to the customer-visible blast radius; ask IC to make final call; document rationale in the incident channel

---

## Ownership
- Primary owner (runbook): Tomáš Novák (Runbooks & oncall readiness)
- Process owner (status comms): Rafael Mendes (SRE)
- Policy owner (disclosure/approval): Dr. Aisha Rahman (Security)

If you find gaps or unclear cases, file an issue in the Status page transparency upgrades epic and tag #eng-sre.
